tagline: Rio's tropical escape hatch — a bay of 365 islands, jungle-fringed beaches, and Ilha Grande just a boat ride away.

taxi.fareNote: Metered in town; boat trips and island transfers are negotiated flat fares, not metered

emergency.note: 190 reaches military police, 192 reaches SAMU (ambulance); response can be slow on the islands

hood_landmark.Centro Histórico: Igreja de Nossa Senhora da Conceição
hood_landmark.Jacuecanga: Marina and ferry terminal to Ilha Grande

hood_desc: Angra's original town center, built around a 16th-century church and a small historic core that survived the city's industrial and naval-shipyard growth. It's the transport hub for buses, the town market, and ferries out to the bay, with a modest walkable strip of shops and eateries.

The car-free village on Ilha Grande, reached only by boat, and the jumping-off point for the island's famous trails and beaches like Lopes Mendes. Sandy paths, pousadas, and seafood shacks replace streets and cars here.
A quieter residential beach neighborhood just outside the center, popular with families and known for its calm bay waters. Fewer tourist crowds than the historic center, with a laid-back, local feel.

An upscale stretch of coastline dotted with gated resort communities, private beach clubs, and Angra's most luxurious hotels, including the Fasano resort. Best suited to travelers who want a resort base rather than a walkable town.

Home to the marina and the main ferry/schooner terminal most visitors use to reach Ilha Grande and the bay's smaller islands. A practical, slightly workaday district built around boat traffic rather than sightseeing.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5am-11pm; boat schedules vary by season and tide
transit.pay: Cash onboard buses; boat tickets and tours purchased at pier kiosks
transit.map: No official transit app; schedules posted at the Jacuecanga and Centro piers
transit.note: Boats (barcos/escunas) are the main way to reach Ilha Grande and the bay's other islands

air: Angra dos Reis Airport (AIA) - small, very limited traffic
bus: Long-distance coaches from Rio's Novo Rio bus station, ~2.5 hours via Costa Verde highway
ferry: Ferries and schooners to Ilha Grande, Vila do Abraão, and other bay islands

tip.r: A 10% service charge is often already included in restaurant bills; additional tipping isn't expected but rounding up is appreciated

tagline: Cambodia's laid-back second city, where French colonial streets meet bamboo trains and hilltop caves.

taxi.fareNote: No metered taxis; tuk-tuk and moto fares are agreed before the ride, or booked via the PassApp Taxi app

emergency.note: Emergency response outside Phnom Penh and Siem Reap can be slow; for serious issues, contact hotel/guesthouse staff and rely on travel medical evacuation insurance

hood_desc: Battambang's best-preserved stretch of French colonial shophouses and villas, lining the Sangkae River in the town center. It's the most walkable part of town, with cafes, galleries, and the starting point for bamboo train and countryside tours.

The Art Deco central market building and the streets around it form Battambang's commercial heart, packed with produce stalls, textiles, and street food. It's the busiest, most local part of the city by day.

A cluster of century-old wooden Khmer houses on stilts just south of downtown, several open to visitors as informal museums. It offers a quiet, rural counterpoint to the town center, best explored by bicycle.

A limestone hill about 12km outside town, topped by a pagoda and home to the sobering Killing Caves, a Khmer Rouge-era memorial site. Bats pour out of a nearby cave at dusk in one of the region's best-known sights.

Home to Prasat Banan, an 11th-century Angkorian-era temple atop a steep 350-step climb, often called a mini Angkor Wat. The surrounding countryside is dotted with rural villages and a small local winery.

transit.pay: Cash (Riel or USD); negotiate fare before riding, or book through the PassApp Taxi app
transit.map: No formal transit map; the PassApp Taxi app covers Battambang
transit.note: There is no public bus or rail network in town; tuk-tuks and motos are the primary way to get around

air: Battambang Airport (BBM) - currently no scheduled commercial flights
train: Cambodia's reactivated Phnom Penh–Poipet line passes through Battambang with very limited passenger service
bus: Frequent buses/vans from Phnom Penh (~5hr), Siem Reap (~3hr), and the Poipet border (~2.5hr)
ferry: Seasonal riverboat to Siem Reap via the Sangkae River and Tonle Sap, wet season only

tip.r: Small tips (5-10%) are appreciated at restaurants; rounding up fares for tuk-tuk and moto drivers is common

tagline: The golden heart of Burgundy, serving Gothic spires, world-class wine, and its namesake mustard.

taxi.fareNote: Official taxis are metered; ranks at the train station and Place Darcy, or call ahead as street hailing is uncommon

emergency.note: 112 works EU-wide for any emergency and reliably connects to English-speaking dispatchers

hood_desc: Dijon's dense, largely pedestrianized old town, built around the Palace of the Dukes of Burgundy and threaded by the Owl's Trail (Parcours de la Chouette). Gothic and Renaissance mansions, the Notre-Dame church, and the covered market Les Halles are all within a short walk.

Once the quarter of wine merchants and boatmen along the Ouche canal, now Dijon's liveliest area for bars, small restaurants, and a lively Saturday market. It retains a rougher, more bohemian edge than the polished old town nearby.
A modern commercial district anchored by the Toison d'Or shopping center, one of the region's largest malls. Mostly of interest for chain shopping and a multiplex cinema rather than sightseeing.
A quiet, largely residential neighborhood northwest of the center, popular with families for its parks and easy tram access. Few tourist sights, but a good gauge of everyday Dijon life.

The university and science-campus district on the city's eastern edge, home to student housing, the botanical Jardin des Sciences, and Dijon's stadium. Quiet outside term time, livelier when students are in session.

transit.pay: DiviaPass card, contactless bank card tap-in, or tickets via the Divia Mobilités app
transit.note: The DIVIA network includes two tram lines (T1, T2) plus extensive bus routes covering greater Dijon

train: Dijon-Ville station: TGV to Paris Gare de Lyon (~1h40), Lyon (~1h40), and Marseille
bus: Flixbus and regional coaches to Lyon, Paris, and other Burgundy towns

airport.name: Paris (CDG/Orly) or Lyon–Saint Exupéry (LYS)
airport.drive: 2.5-3 hours by car, or 1h40 by TGV from Paris

tip.r: Service is included in listed prices (service compris); rounding up or leaving small change is a nice gesture, not required

tagline: Gateway to the emerald limestone karsts of UNESCO-listed Ha Long Bay

taxi.color: green and white (Mai Linh) or turquoise (Halong Taxi)
taxi.fareNote: Stick to reputable companies like Mai Linh; use the Grab app to avoid overcharging, which is common with unmetered street taxis near the bay.

emergency.note: Fire is 114. English-speaking assistance may be limited; for serious medical issues, transfer to Hanoi is common.

hood_desc: The main tourist district on the western shore of Ha Long Bay, packed with hotels, seafood restaurants, and the Sun World Ha Long Complex cable car and amusement park. The lively Ha Long Night Market draws visitors for souvenirs and street food each evening. Most bay cruises depart from the nearby international cruise port.

The older, more local half of the city across the bay from Bai Chay, home to the municipal offices, the central market, and the port. It offers a grittier, more authentic slice of daily Vietnamese life away from the resort crowds.

A man-made peninsula turned resort island connected by a causeway, home to a large marina, a water park, and many of the wooden junk boats used for overnight bay cruises. It has a resort-town feel with hotels, restaurants, and evening entertainment.
A quieter district built around the revered Cua Ong Temple, a hillside pilgrimage site dedicated to a 13th-century general. It sees more domestic pilgrims than foreign tourists and has a slower pace.
A relaxed residential and beach area near Bai Chay, with a public beach, small seafood shacks, and fewer crowds than the main tourist strip. It's popular with locals for weekend swims.
lodging: Ha Long Bay View Hotel Tuan Chau
Wyndham Garden Ha Long Bay Tuan Chau
FLC Halong Bay Golf Club & Luxury Resort

transit.map: no official transit app; Grab recommended
transit.note: Most visitors rely on hotel transfers, taxis, or Grab; walking along the Bai Chay and Hon Gai waterfronts is common.

train: No direct rail; nearest station is Hanoi, ~180km away
bus: Frequent buses and limousine vans from Hanoi (~2.5-3.5 hrs)
ferry: Boats and cruises depart from Tuan Chau Marina and Ha Long International Cruise Port for bay tours

airport.name: Van Don International Airport (VDO)
rentals: Limited local operators; hotel transfers common

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in Vietnam, but rounding up or 5-10% for good service in tourist restaurants is appreciated; tour guides and boat crews often expect a small tip.

tagline: Nicaragua's colonial heart, all cathedral bells, murals, and volcano views

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are often shared (colectivo-style) and unmetered; agree on the fare before getting in, typically 25-40 córdobas within the center.

emergency.note: Response times can be slow; private clinics such as Hospital San Vicente offer faster care than public hospitals for travelers.

hood_landmark.Centro Histórico: Catedral de la Asunción de León (UNESCO)
hood_landmark.Sutiaba: Iglesia San Juan Bautista de Sutiaba
hood_landmark.Barrio Guadalupe: Iglesia de Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe

hood_desc: León's UNESCO-listed colonial core, centered on the massive whitewashed Catedral de la Asunción de León, the largest cathedral in Central America. Cobblestone streets, revolutionary murals, and the Rubén Darío House Museum surround the central Parque Jerez. Most restaurants, hostels, and historic churches are within walking distance.

León's oldest neighborhood, an indigenous barrio predating the Spanish colonial city, centered on the 17th-century Iglesia San Juan Bautista. It retains a distinct cultural identity with its own patron saint festivals and craft traditions.

A quieter residential district anchored by the Iglesia de San Felipe, with tree-lined streets and traditional single-story colonial homes. It's a good base for travelers wanting a calmer, more local pace close to the center.

A working neighborhood with a busy local market and the colorful Iglesia de Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe, popular for cheap eats and everyday Nicaraguan life. Fewer tourists venture here than the historic core.

Home to UNAN-León, one of Nicaragua's oldest universities, this district has a youthful energy with student bars, cheap food stalls, and the lively Calle de los Poetas nearby. It's the epicenter of León's modest but real nightlife scene.

transit.note: Bicycles and pedicabs (bicitaxis) are common for getting around the compact colonial center.

train: No passenger rail service in Nicaragua
bus: Frequent minibuses and express buses to/from Managua (~1.5-2 hrs)

tip.r: Tipping isn't deeply ingrained; 10% in sit-down restaurants is appreciated and sometimes already added as a service charge, and rounding up for taxis is common.

tagline: A romantic canal town of glass, music boxes, and fresh Hokkaido seafood

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are reliable and metered but expensive by Western standards; most useful late at night or when carrying luggage in winter.

emergency.note: Japan's emergency services are fast and reliable; English support is improving but not guaranteed outside major hospitals.

hood_desc: The city's postcard image: a restored 1920s canal lined with old stone warehouses, gas lamps, and willow trees, especially atmospheric when lit up at night. It's the most-photographed spot in Otaru and the heart of the tourist district.

A preserved Meiji- and Taisho-era merchant street lined with former banks and trading houses, now selling music boxes, hand-blown glass, and Otaru's famous sushi and soft-serve ice cream. It's the main shopping strip for souvenirs and crafts.

The transit hub of the city, anchored by JR Otaru Station's landmark 1934 building with its gas-lamp motif interior. Shops, izakayas, and easy access to Sapporo trains make it a practical, central base.

A quieter residential area built around the former Temiya rail line, Hokkaido's first railway, now preserved as a walking and cycling path. It offers a low-key, local slice of Otaru away from the canal crowds.

A former herring-fishing district on Otaru's coast, home to the Otaru Aquarium and the preserved Nishin Goten herring mansion. Its rocky coastline and small beaches make it a relaxed spot for sea views.

transit.note: Otaru Station connects to Sapporo in about 30-40 minutes by train; the historic canal area itself is compact and walkable.

train: JR Hakodate Main Line links Otaru directly to Sapporo and New Chitose Airport
bus: Chuo Bus connects Otaru to Sapporo and the airport
ferry: New Otaru Ferry Terminal serves long-distance ferries to Maizuru and Niigata

tip.r: Tipping is not practiced in Japan and can even be considered rude or confusing; excellent service is simply the norm.

tagline: Historic Ghanaian coastal city anchored by a UNESCO slave-trade fortress and golden Atlantic beaches.

taxi.fareNote: Shared taxis and tro-tros are cheap but unmetered; agree on a fare before you get in. Private taxis for tourists should also be negotiated up front.

emergency.note: The unified national emergency line 112 also connects to police, fire, and ambulance services; response times outside Accra can be slow.

hood_landmark.Victoria Park: Jubilee Park & Cape Coast Methodist Cathedral

hood_desc: The civic heart of Cape Coast, centered on Victoria Park and the old colonial-era buildings lining Commercial Street; the easiest base for reaching the castle, the market, and onward transport.
Home to Cape Coast Castle, the UNESCO-listed fortress central to the transatlantic slave trade, and the fishing harbor beside it, lined with pastel colonial buildings and busy fishing canoes.
The city's largest and liveliest market, rebuilt in recent years, where traders sell cloth, produce, and fresh fish; a good place to see everyday Cape Coast life.
A quieter residential suburb inland from the historic center, popular with families and increasingly with guesthouses catering to volunteers and students.
Home to the University of Cape Coast, with a younger, livelier feel thanks to student bars, cheap eats, and a beachfront campus.

transit.hours: Roughly 5am-8pm, with limited service after dark
transit.pay: Cash only, paid directly to the driver or mate
transit.map: No official transit map; routes are learned locally
transit.note: No public bus network or metro; tro-tros and shared or private taxis are the main way to get around.

bus: STC and VIP long-distance buses connect Cape Coast to Accra, Takoradi, and Kumasi

tip.r: 5-10% at tourist-oriented restaurants is appreciated; not expected at small local eateries. Guides at Cape Coast Castle and Kakum National Park often expect a modest tip.

tagline: Colonial silver-mining city beneath the legendary Cerro Rico, one of the highest cities on Earth.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis are unmetered; agree a price before departure. Shared 'trufis' running fixed routes are the cheapest way to get around.

emergency.note: Response times can be slow at this altitude; for serious issues go directly to a private clinic and contact your embassy.

hood_desc: The colonial core of Potosí, a UNESCO World Heritage Site built on silver wealth, packed with baroque churches, balconied mansions, and the Casa de la Moneda mint museum.
A quieter colonial quarter around the Convento de San Francisco, known for rooftop views over the city's red-tiled roofs to Cerro Rico.
The mining district at the foot of the legendary 'mountain that eats men,' where cooperative miners still work largely by hand; guided (and physically demanding) mine tours start from here.
A working-class residential neighborhood with a strong local feel, well away from the tourist circuit.
Potosí's central market area, crowded with stalls selling produce, coca leaves, and household goods; a good spot for cheap local food.

transit.map: No official transit map; routes are fixed but informal
transit.note: No metro; trufis and micros cover the city cheaply, and the compact historic center is very walkable (altitude permitting).

bus: Long-distance buses connect Potosí to Sucre (about 3 hours), La Paz (about 10 hours), and Uyuni (about 3-4 hours)

tip.r: Tipping isn't customary but rounding up or leaving small change is appreciated; mine-tour guides usually expect a modest tip.

tagline: Bohemian English seaside city famous for its pier, Regency architecture, and LGBTQ+-friendly nightlife.

taxi.fareNote: Licensed black cabs and private hire minicabs run on metered or pre-agreed fares; Uber is widely available.

emergency.note: Dial 999 for police, fire, or ambulance in a genuine emergency; 101 for non-emergency police and 111 for NHS non-emergency medical advice.

hood_desc: A maze of narrow medieval alleyways in the old fishing quarter, now packed with jewelers, antique shops, and cafes, with the Royal Pavilion just to the north.
Brighton's bohemian shopping district, full of independent boutiques, vintage stores, vegan cafes, and street art near the station-to-seafront axis.
The heart of Brighton's LGBTQ+ scene along St James's Street, with a dense cluster of bars, clubs, and drag venues alongside elegant Regency squares.
Brighton's more genteel western neighbor, with grand Regency terraces, wide lawns along the seafront, and a calmer pace than the city center.
The promenade running from the Palace Pier to the i360 tower, with the beach, arcades, and the burnt-out skeleton of the old West Pier.

transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5am-midnight with some night services on key routes; trains run until around midnight
transit.pay: Contactless bank card, the Brighton & Hove Buses app, or PayPoint travel cards
transit.note: No underground or metro; buses and trains cover the city and region, and the center itself is very walkable and bikeable.

train: Direct trains to London Victoria and London St Pancras International (about 1 hour), plus coastal lines to Portsmouth, Hastings, and Southampton
bus: National Express coaches to London and regional towns

car.idp: Not required for short US/EU visits

tip.r: A 10-12.5% service charge is often added automatically at restaurants; tipping taxis or bars isn't expected, though rounding up is common.
